what_it_is.prose: IAI is Israel's largest state-owned aerospace and defence company and one of India's most established foreign OEM partners, with a documented 30-year strategic relationship. It has executed multi-billion-dollar Indian contracts spanning AWACS (EL/W-2090 on IL-76), Barak-8 naval air defence (LR-SAM, $777M, 2018) jointly with DRDO/BEL, and the Heron family of MALE UAVs (Heron Mk-II, Heron TP). IAI Harop loitering munitions were used by India during Operation Sindoor (May 2025) against Pakistani air-defence targets, and India has initiated procurement of additional Heron Mk-II post-Sindoor (Dec 2025). IAI has a New Delhi subsidiary (Aerospace Services India / ASI, opened 2022, operational 2024) for life-cycle support of air-defence systems, and a new JV with DCX (Apr 2025) for loitering munitions. Combined backlog exposure to India was disclosed in IAI's 2023 annual report as a material portion of its $30B+ order backlog.

faq.question: What is IAI's largest India defence contract?
faq.answer: IAI's largest single disclosed India contract is the $777 million Barak-8 LR-SAM deal signed with BEL on 24 October 2018 for the Indian Navy's air-defence missile systems; an additional $93M follow-on for missile deliveries was signed in February 2019.

faq.question: Does IAI have a subsidiary in India?
faq.answer: Yes. IAI announced a wholly-owned Indian subsidiary, AeroSpace Services India (ASI), based in New Delhi, in October 2022; it was formally operationalised in 2024 to provide product life-cycle support for IAI's air-defence systems in India under the Make in India programme.

faq.question: Did India use IAI Harop drones during Operation Sindoor?
faq.answer: Yes. IAI Harop loitering munitions (in Indian inventory since the late 2000s) were reportedly used during Operation Sindoor in May 2025 to strike Pakistani air-defence targets around Lahore, prompting India to move to procure additional Heron Mk-II UAVs post-conflict (December 2025).
